Thanks Alex — this is very helpful. Attached are two short artifacts to review ahead of the follow-up:

- fastretail_cost_model_reserved_vs_api.xlsx (spreadsheet) — sample cost scenarios for 20M and 40M tokens comparing Hosted per-token, Dedicated reserved commit, and Dedicated with burst capacity.
- redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf (one-pager) — explanation of commit tiers, typical mapping guidance, and overage policies.

High-level notes (short answers to your asks):
1) Hosted API: per-token pricing is simplest to start and scales linearly — for your 20M baseline you’d see predictable per-token costs but no capacity reservation (good for experimentation).
2) Dedicated reserved commit: you pay a monthly reserved capacity to guarantee GPUs and throughput. Break-even vs hosted usually happens around medium-volume workloads (often ~10–30M tokens/month depending on model and quantization) — the spreadsheet has example break-evens using gpt-like models and our typical batching assumptions.
3) Burst handling: Dedicated customers can configure a burst buffer (pay-as-you-go burst) or set policy to fall back to hosted model variants during short spikes. Overage pricing is typically blended (delta of committed unit price + short-term capacity premium); details in the attached PDF.

Next step: Aditya can run through the numbers and sizing mapping — are you available Thu 3/26 10:00am PT? If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and include Maria + procurement.

Thanks,
Neha
